translation.english_title: Riding the chariot called the breeze

source_tamil_lines: ஆ... தென்றல் என்னும் தேர் ஏறி - தமிழ்
english_lines: Aa... riding the chariot called the breeze — O mullai flower,
Who came to the Tamil mandram,
Riding the chariot called the breeze — O mullai flower,
Who came to the Tamil mandram,
There is no beauty like you,
Transform like the rising `nyaayirene`,
Come, come as light to awaken the world!
(Breeze).
notes: `முல்லை` and `தமிழ் மன்றம்` remain culturally audible as `mullai` and `Tamil mandram` rather than being generalized.
The verified `ஞாயிறெனெ` is retained conservatively as `nyaayirene`; the English does not silently regularize the Tamil to a familiar `sun-like` form.

english_lines: I know all the wisdom of music,
Nasika Poosani is the raga I sing,
I know all the wisdom of music,
Nasika Poosani is the raga I sing,
To utter jathi with bhava and sing —
That ability too comes with it,
I too am the one who knows, am I not?
I know the depth of many books,
(Breeze).
notes: `நாசிகா பூசனி` remains `Nasika Poosani` as printed, without substituting an externally familiar raga name.
`பாவம் / ஜதி` remain `bhava / jathi`, preserving the performance vocabulary and the boastful comic register.

english_lines: Thagath thom-thillanaa,
Thagath thom-thillanaa — (jathi utterance),
Thom... thom...
Your face cools like a cool moon,
Your inner self boils like burning heat,
The song of the great Madurai Tamil Sangam,
Hearing honey-sweet lips sing it,
Pluck the veena till honey flows into the ear,
Who in the world — show me.
notes: The jathi vocables are transliterated rather than replaced by English sound effects.
The final verified `உலகிலே யார் காட்டு` remains deliberately abrupt; the English does not invent a missing object or completion.

translator_notes: The song mixes Tamil-cultural address, comic musical self-display, technical performance vocabulary and sensual imagery; the English retains those registers side by side.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
